units.name: Comprehension
units.passage:
**Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow.**

> The habit of sustained reading is not a natural endowment but an acquired discipline, and like every discipline it is sustained by a community rather than by solitary resolve. A reader who has nobody to talk to about what she reads will, sooner or later, read less. This is why the decline of reading in our time is not primarily a failure of individual will; it is a failure of shared attention. We have built institutions that reward the accumulation of information and punish the slowness in which understanding grows. The examination measures what can be recalled in an hour; the classroom, pressed for time, teaches what can be measured. Meanwhile the student learns the most durable lesson of all — that a book is an obstacle standing between herself and her marks. Nothing will change until teachers are permitted to be slow. A curriculum that has room for silence, for re-reading, and for the honest admission that a text has not yet been understood is not a luxury added to education; it is the condition under which education becomes possible at all.

questions.stem: According to the passage, the habit of sustained reading is:
options: An inborn gift possessed by a few
An acquired discipline sustained by a community
Purely an achievement of solitary will
A by-product of the examination system

questions.stem: The author holds that the decline of reading is primarily:
options: The result of an absence of books

questions.stem: According to the passage, the classroom teaches what can be measured because:
options: Measurement is the true aim of education

questions.stem: The idea that a book is an obstacle between the student and her marks is described in the passage as:
options: The most durable lesson the student learns
The private opinion of the teacher
An argument in favour of more frequent examinations

questions.stem: The author regards room for silence and re-reading in the curriculum as:
options: The condition that makes education possible
A concession made to weaker students
An obstacle to the coverage of the syllabus

units.passage:
**Read the following lines and answer the questions that follow.**

> So this is what the crown weighs: not the gold,
> But every hand I struck to hold it up.
> I told myself the kingdom needed me;
> The lie was well made, and it wore my face.
> Now in the glass my father's eyes look out
> And ask me, gently, what I have become.
> I have become the argument I made
> Against the men I hanged for making it.
> There is no hour left in which to be
> The man I promised, in my youth, to be;
> And yet the morning comes as if it could,
> And birds outside my window keep their trust.
> I would give back the years, if years were coin.
> They are not. What is done is architecture:
> I live in it. The doors are of my making.
> Even this remorse is furniture I bought.

units.passage:
**Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.**

> Criticism is often described as a parasite upon creation, and the description is accepted too meekly by critics themselves. But the relation is not one of dependence merely. A poem that no one has read attentively is, for practical purposes, a poem that does not yet exist; the act of reading well is itself a kind of composition, performed in a different medium and to a different end. This does not license the critic to substitute her own invention for the text, for the discipline of criticism lies precisely in refusing that liberty. The critic's freedom is the freedom of the translator: enormous within a boundary, and worthless outside it. What she may not do is decide in advance what the work will be found to mean and then arrange the evidence accordingly. Where that happens, criticism becomes a branch of autobiography, and usually a dull one. The measure of good criticism is therefore not originality alone, but the amount of the text it can hold in view without distortion.

questions.stem: The author's attitude towards the claim that criticism is a parasite upon creation is one of:
In saying that reading well is itself a kind of composition, the author means that:
options: Critics ought also to write poems

options: Freedom exercised within a strict boundary

options: The amount of the text it can hold in view without distortion
